data.title: Churchill Downs Seeks $500 Million Loan Refinance
data.description:
Churchill Downs Inc., the Kentucky Derby operator, is seeking to raise $500 million to refinance existing debt as maturities approach, according to Bloomberg.

The move adds to a rush of companies tapping the market for risky loans.

data.title: FamilyMart To Launch AI-Conceived Dessert This Month
data.description: According to Nikkei Asia, Japanese convenience store chain FamilyMart will launch a dessert conceived by artificial intelligence later this month as part of an effort to use generative AI to develop new products and capture consumer trends.

data.title: STOCKS | Defiance Seeks SEC Approval for Hourly Leveraged Stock ETFs
data.description:
Defiance ETFs has filed paperwork with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission for a series of leveraged funds designed to double the moves of some individual stocks over periods measured in hours, according to Bloomberg.

The filing comes as a corner of the ETF market already drawing regulatory scrutiny pushes for even shorter-term speculation.

data.title: FCA and Bank of England to Develop Tokenization Roadmap After 123 Responses
data.description:
The U.K. Financial Conduct Authority and the Bank of England will develop a tokenization roadmap based on feedback from 123 responses. According to NS3.AI, most respondents identified post-trade processes as the main opportunity for adoption.

The roadmap is expected later this year and will set target dates for the U.K.'s wholesale tokenization work.

data.title: Saudi Arabia Seeks British Military and Diplomatic Support Against Houthi Offensive
data.description:
British Prime Minister Burnham is considering whether to help Saudi Arabia defend against attacks by Yemen's Houthi movement. According to Sina Finance, people familiar with the matter said Burnham has received a series of Saudi requests for diplomatic and military support.

The requests include operational support for Saudi forces to push back the Iran-backed group as it advances along Yemen's Red Sea coast toward the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, as well as help defending against attacks on Saudi oil infrastructure. It is unclear whether Burnham is willing to approve the requests, and the British government has not disclosed them. A spokesperson said Britain will work with partners to support regional stability.

data.title: Anthropic Co-Founder Says AI Kill Switch May Need To Be Mandatory
data.description:
Anthropic co-founder Jack Clark said companies may eventually need a mandatory, third-party-verifiable AI “kill switch” to shut software down if it becomes too dangerous, according to BBC. He said most AI labs already have ways to “pull the plug”, but argued policymakers may need to require such safeguards as part of a wider policy debate around AI safety.

Clark’s comments come as Anthropic and other AI firms face growing scrutiny over the risks of advanced systems. Anthropic head Dario Amodei has also called for AI development to slow and be more closely monitored, while US lawmakers have proposed the Kill Switch Act, which would require companies to be able to shut down problematic AI tools. The UK government has recently rejected the idea of a kill switch, saying it would not stop systems being developed or misused elsewhere.

data.title: AI Control Fears Intensify After Advances and Cybersecurity Breaches
data.description:
Fears that artificial intelligence could escape human control have grown in recent days as the technology advances, according to Bloomberg.

The concerns have been driven by a series of cybersecurity breaches involving AI agents and new warnings from rank-and-file AI staffers.

data.title: Iran's Revolutionary Guards Navy Says Super Tanker Hit Mine, Exploded Near Strait of Hormuz
data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, Iran's Revolutionary Guards Navy said the super tanker Al-Ghayah hit a mine while trying to cross a prohibited zone south of the Strait of Hormuz and then exploded, with firefighting efforts failing and the vessel catching fire.

data.title: Patrick Witt Says He Feels "Very Good" About Senate's Initial Clarity Act Vote
data.description:
White House crypto adviser Patrick Witt said he feels "very good" about the Senate's initial vote on the Clarity Act. According to NS3.AI, the Senate is scheduled to hold the procedural vote on Tuesday, and the bill needs 60 votes to advance.

The legislation would regulate the cryptocurrency industry at the federal level for the first time.

data.title: Bank of America’s Moynihan Says AI Firms Are Taking Safety Seriously
data.description:
Bank of America Chairman and CEO Brian Moynihan said it is "encouraging" that AI firms are taking AI safety seriously as leaders warn about the pace of innovation and possible ramifications, according to Bloomberg.

Moynihan told Bloomberg's Dani Burger he expects trading to be "relatively flat" in the third quarter compared with last year.

data.title: UN Iran Fact-Finding Mission Urges U.S. and Israel to Comply With International Law
data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, the UN Independent International Fact-Finding Mission on Iran on the 14th urged the United States and Israel to comply with international law, condemned recent U.S. airstrikes on Iran for failing to take necessary measures and causing civilian deaths, and called for an assessment of the incidents to ensure victims receive justice and compensation.

data.title: S&P 500, Nasdaq Rebound as 10-Year Treasury Yield Tops 5%
data.description: According to CNBC, the S&P 500 and Nasdaq fell Monday on AI safety concerns before recovering from their session lows as the 10-year Treasury yield briefly topped 5%, a level not seen since October 2023. Buyers stepped in at that yield, pushing Treasury prices higher and yields lower, while oil prices trimmed earlier gains; West Texas Intermediate crude still settled above $100 per barrel. Market odds of an interest-rate hike at the Federal Reserve's two-day September meeting on Tuesday and Wednesday were above 92%, according to the CME FedWatch tool. AI infrastructure stocks led declines after Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei's weekend essay called for an industry-wide slowdown in the development of new AI models. CrowdStrike and Palo Alto Networks rose about 14% each, while Meta Platforms, Alphabet and Microsoft gained on expectations that a slower AI buildout could reduce capital spending pressure.

data.title: Fed Extends Treasury Bill Purchase Pause to Mid-October
data.description:
The Federal Reserve said Monday it will not buy Treasury bills for reserve management purposes in the upcoming period, marking a second straight month without such purchases, according to Bloomberg.

The central bank said the decision suggests policymakers are comfortable with the level of bank reserves in the financial system.

data.title: US President Donald Trump Says Inflation Was Caused by Biden, Predicts Oil Prices Will Fall
data.description:
US President Donald Trump said he wants everyone to recognize that rising prices across the United States were caused by Biden and his administration, not by "Trump." According to Sina Finance, he said oil prices were higher during Biden's term than they are now, and that he had prevented Iran from obtaining nuclear weapons.

Trump said prices are falling sharply except for a temporary exception in oil prices. He added that once the military conflict with Iran ends, oil prices will plunge, and that day is not far away.

data.title: JD Vance: About 870,000 People Accused of Misusing Taxpayer Funds Barred From Federal Loans
data.description: U.S. Vice President JD Vance said the federal government will end related eligibility and stop providing support to anyone who harms U.S. taxpayers. According to Sina Finance, the government will revoke the ability of about 870,000 people to apply for federal loans after they were accused of stealing taxpayer funds. Vance said those people will no longer be able to apply for such loans and called the move "very reasonable." Even if they submit applications, they will not receive those benefits.
